decisive_items: retrograde ureterography revealed a ureteroileal fistula
response.rationale: Ureteroileal fistula was directly confirmed by retrograde ureterography, a specific finding that explains recurrent hematuria in the setting of prior pelvic radiation and surgery. Other candidates either localize bleeding to the bladder (R1, R7) or are non-specific (R4, R5, R3, R6).

rejected.why: Ureteral stricture explains hydronephrosis but not the arterial bleeding.
Cancer-related hemorrhage is too vague and not supported by imaging.
Hemorrhagic cystitis is bladder-localized, while bleeding is from the ureteral orifice.
Radiation-induced hemorrhagic cystitis also localizes to the bladder, not the upper tract.
Infectious complication is not the cause of the arterial hemorrhage.
Candida glabrata infection is a prior complication, not the current bleeding source.
